paragraphs: High-resolution visual encoders help multimodal models recognize fine details, but processing all their image tokens is expensive. Removing tokens can save computation, yet charts present a particular problem: important structure may occupy only small, isolated regions. A pruning rule that works on natural photographs can therefore discard information essential to interpreting a structured image.

AD-BTS chooses between two processing branches according to the image’s spatial information density. A lightweight gate examines pixel gradients to estimate how flat or structurally varied the input is. One branch aggressively removes redundant tokens while keeping the encoder frozen. The other uses conditional LoRA adaptation and context fusion to preserve sparse structural information.

Experiments with Qwen2.5-VL report an improved tradeoff between accuracy and computation. With 20% of tokens retained, AD-BTS outperforms the strongest baseline by 12.1% on ChartQA and achieves a 1.8× prefill speedup. These results support adapting the compression strategy to the input’s structure, rather than applying the same token-selection behavior to every image.
icml-2026-ad-bts-adaptive-dual-branch-to.tldr: AD-BTS routes images through different token-compression branches to preserve sparse visual structure while reducing computation.

paragraphs: Graph-based retrieval systems organize information into entities and connections so they can answer questions requiring several reasoning steps. Their effectiveness can depend heavily on which connections were recorded. When a knowledge graph contains noise or missing edges, following its existing links may lead reasoning away from useful evidence or leave relevant information disconnected.

INSES combines two ways of navigating this imperfect structure. A language model guides exploration and filters noise, while embedding similarity expands the search beyond explicit edges. The latter provides a way to bridge semantic gaps when related information lacks a recorded connection. A lightweight router sends simpler questions to ordinary retrieval-augmented generation and reserves INSES for more complex cases.

The experiments report favorable performance against established RAG and GraphRAG baselines across multiple benchmarks. On MINE, the method also shows robustness across knowledge graphs built using different construction methods. The findings support combining graph navigation with semantic search, while the router addresses the computational cost of using deeper graph reasoning for every query.
icml-2026-beyond-explicit-edges-robust-r.tldr: INSES combines language-model-guided graph navigation with semantic similarity search to reason over noisy and incomplete knowledge graphs.

paragraphs: Processing long sequences is expensive for language models because self-attention has a quadratic cost in sequence length. Caracal replaces this component with a parameter-efficient Multi-Head Fourier module. It uses the Fast Fourier Transform to mix information across a sequence, with a stated computational cost of O(L log L), and addresses limitations associated with positional encodings.

The central architectural challenge is preserving causal generation: a prediction must not use future tokens. Caracal introduces a frequency-domain causal masking technique implemented through asymmetric padding and truncation. This makes Fourier-based sequence mixing compatible with autoregressive modeling, where the model generates a sequence by predicting successive tokens from the available past.

The architecture uses standard library operators rather than depending on hardware-specific implementations, which the authors present as a portability advantage. Evaluations show competitive performance against Transformer and state-space-model baselines. The contribution is thus a combination of efficient sequence mixing, a mechanism for causal generation, and a comparatively simple implementation route for long-sequence models.
icml-2026-caracal-causal-architecture-vi.tldr: Caracal replaces self-attention with causal Fourier mixing to support efficient, portable long-sequence language modeling.

paragraphs: Estimating conditional average treatment effects means learning how an intervention’s average effect varies with observed characteristics. Obtaining outcome measurements can be costly, so an active-learning system must decide which measurements are most useful. The paper argues that reducing uncertainty about model parameters or observed outcomes can miss the causal quantity the researcher actually wants to estimate.

Causal-EPIG adapts expected predictive information gain to target uncertainty in causal quantities directly. It develops two acquisition strategies: one considers the joint structure of potential outcomes, while the other focuses specifically on the treatment-effect estimate. These choices represent different ways to direct data collection toward the causal estimation objective.

The authors establish a theoretical connection between treatment-effect estimation error and posterior uncertainty in causal quantities. Experiments show better sample efficiency than standard baselines, but they also show that the preferred strategy depends on the underlying estimator and treatment-effect structure. The practical contribution is a principled framework for choosing informative measurements, with the choice between its two strategies remaining context-dependent.
icml-2026-causal-epig-causally-aligned-a.tldr: Causal-EPIG selects outcome measurements by targeting uncertainty in treatment effects or potential outcomes directly.

paragraphs: A robot world model predicts how an environment will change in response to actions. Learning such a model for varied, dexterous interactions is difficult because robot datasets cover limited situations and action labels are scarce. DreamDojo learns from 44,000 hours of human videos recorded from the wearer’s perspective, covering everyday objects, skills, and interactions.

To use videos without explicit action labels, the method introduces continuous latent actions as a shared proxy for actions. These representations support transferring interaction knowledge from human video into the robot model. After further training on a small amount of target-robot data, the authors report strong physical understanding and precise control of simulated outcomes through actions.

A distillation pipeline accelerates generation to 10.93 frames per second while improving consistency with the supplied context. Evaluations on several challenging out-of-distribution benchmarks support the method’s usefulness for simulating contact-rich interactions. The resulting model enables applications including live teleoperation, policy evaluation, and model-based planning, connecting broad video pretraining to action-conditioned robot simulation.
icml-2026-dreamdojo-a-generalist-robot-w.tldr: DreamDojo learns robot world simulation from large-scale human video using latent actions, then adapts to target robots.

paragraphs: Language-model serving has two phases with different resource demands. Prefill processes the input and is compute-intensive, while decoding generates successive tokens and is constrained by memory access. Sharing a GPU can let prefill interfere with decoding, increasing the delay between tokens. Separating the phases across GPUs introduces duplicated models and transfers of cached information.

DuetServe normally runs both phases together, but predicts when contention will threaten the required time between tokens. It then partitions the GPU’s streaming multiprocessors to isolate the phases within the same device. An attention-aware performance model forecasts iteration latency, and an optimizer chooses a partition intended to maximize throughput while meeting the latency constraint.

The framework also includes an execution engine that eliminates CPU–GPU synchronization overhead without interrupting execution. Evaluations report up to 1.3× higher total throughput than state-of-the-art serving frameworks while maintaining low generation latency. The main idea is to activate isolation when needed, allowing resource sharing and latency protection to coexist within a single GPU.
icml-2026-duetserve-harmonizing-prefill-.tldr: DuetServe adaptively partitions a single GPU to protect token-generation latency while maintaining high serving throughput.

paragraphs: Assessing the emotions an image evokes requires more than assigning a broad emotion label. The paper targets multiple emotional attributes, differences in intensity, and the reasoning needed to explain an assessment. It introduces both a dataset and a multimodal language model to address the coarse emotion perception and limited reasoning of existing approaches.

The dataset, EEmoDB, covers five analysis dimensions across five task categories. Its question-answering portion contains 1.2 million automatically generated pairs based on 125,000 images. A separate assessment portion contains 36,000 examples curated from 25,000 images. Together, these components support emotion-related questions and more detailed assessment within a unified resource.

EEmo-Logic is trained through instruction fine-tuning followed by task-customized group relative preference optimization with a new reward design. Experiments report robust results on both in-domain and cross-domain datasets, including strong emotion question answering and fine-grained assessment. The work connects broader training coverage with task-specific optimization to improve how a single model describes and reasons about image-evoked emotion.
icml-2026-eemo-logic-a-unified-dataset-a.tldr: EEmo-Logic combines a large emotion-understanding dataset with staged model training for detailed assessment of image-evoked emotions.

paragraphs: The key-value cache stores information used by attention during language-model generation, and its memory requirements become a bottleneck with long contexts. Compression reduces this footprint, but assigning equal or fixed retention budgets overlooks differences between attention heads. EntroKV instead asks which heads are most sensitive to losing cached information.

Its allocation rule uses attention entropy as a proxy for that sensitivity. High-entropy attention is more spread out, and the authors find that these heads need larger retention budgets. Low-entropy heads can tolerate more aggressive compression without accuracy degradation in the reported analysis. The framework adjusts budgets across layers, heads, and tasks in real time and can work with different compression operators.

Experiments show consistent improvements over the tested baselines, retaining approximately 98% of full-cache performance with a 30% budget ratio and negligible computational overhead. This result concerns the reported performance measure relative to a full cache. The contribution is a lightweight scheduling mechanism that directs limited cache capacity toward the attention components that need it most.
icml-2026-entrokv-entropy-guided-dynamic.tldr: EntroKV dynamically allocates cache capacity using attention entropy, retaining about 98% of full-cache performance at a 30% budget.

paragraphs: Neural wave functions can represent ground and excited quantum states accurately, but handling many states increases the cost of estimating their overlaps. In Variational Monte Carlo, obtaining sufficiently accurate overlap estimates typically requires more samples as the number of states grows. The paper addresses both the sampling burden and the cost of evaluating multiple states.

Multi-State Importance Sampling reuses samples from all states to estimate pairwise overlaps, allowing a nearly constant sample size. The accompanying Excited Pfaffians architecture represents many states within one neural network, making it efficient to evaluate every state on those samples. It also supports multi-state potential energy surfaces within a single model.

For the carbon dimer, the method matches natural excited states with O(N_s^4) scaling while training over 200 times faster and modeling 50% more states. The authors also report using neural networks to find all distinct energy levels of the beryllium atom and representing excited states across multiple molecules with one wave function. These results demonstrate the value of combining shared sampling with shared state representations.
icml-2026-excited-pfaffians-generalized-.tldr: Excited Pfaffians combines shared neural representations and multi-state sampling to make modeling many quantum states more efficient.

paragraphs: Determining whether media was generated by a machine and determining whether its message is true are separate questions. FakeWorld 1.0 brings them into one benchmark because deceptive material can exploit both at once. Its evaluation covers media authenticity alongside factual correctness and consistency between different types of content.

The benchmark includes synthesized text, audio, images, and video. It pairs this coverage with factual errors and semantic mismatches across modalities, presenting examples in web-based and streaming-style settings. These settings preserve the surrounding context in which deception is encountered. Each example also includes an explanatory rationale, supporting analysis of why a particular item should be judged deceptive.

Tests of open- and closed-source multimodal language models reveal capability limits in detecting realistic deception that combines different sources and media types. The paper also introduces OmniChecker, an agentic framework that jointly assesses both dimensions and produces diagnostic reports backed by evidence. Together, the benchmark and framework make explanations part of evaluating deception, rather than reducing the task to a single unexplained label.
icml-2026-fakeworld-1-0-an-omni-modal-be.tldr: FakeWorld evaluates both media authenticity and content truthfulness across text, audio, images, and video in realistic presentation settings.

paragraphs: Pearl’s Causal Hierarchy distinguishes statements about observations, interventions, and counterfactuals. Satisfiability asks whether a collection of such statements can hold together in a causal model. This is computationally intractable in almost all classical settings considered by the paper, motivating a closer look at which structural features make particular cases manageable.

The authors use parameterized complexity to separate overall problem size from parameters such as the number of variables and primal treewidth, a measure of structural interconnectedness. They obtain fixed-parameter and XP algorithms for selected probabilistic and counterfactual fragments. These are distinct forms of parameter-dependent tractability, rather than a claim that general causal satisfiability has become easy.

Matching hardness results delineate where those algorithmic improvements stop applying. Technically, the methods exploit structural descriptions of well-formed causal models instead of the dynamic programming commonly used for treewidth-based algorithms. The contribution is both a map of tractable cases and a different algorithmic toolkit for checking whether causal statements are mutually compatible.
icml-2026-gateways-to-tractability-for-s.tldr: The paper identifies parameter-dependent tractable cases for causal satisfiability and proves hardness results marking their limits.

paragraphs: Training spatially capable models requires detailed information about three-dimensional scenes. Existing approaches often generate questions from a limited collection of manually annotated datasets, restricting scale and exposing models to narrow domains. Holi-Spatial instead introduces a fully automated pipeline that constructs spatially annotated data directly from raw videos without human intervention.

The pipeline supplies several levels of supervision: 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions and rendered depth maps, object annotations, relationships, and spatial questions. Its Holi-Spatial-4M dataset contains 12,000 optimized scenes, 1.3 million 2D masks, 320,000 3D bounding boxes, and 320,000 instance captions. It also includes 1.2 million 3D grounding instances and 1.2 million spatial question-answer pairs.

Evaluations report higher data-curation quality than existing feed-forward and per-scene optimized methods on datasets including ScanNet, ScanNet++, and DL3DV. Fine-tuning vision-language models with the resulting spatial data substantially improves their performance. The work links automated scene reconstruction with semantic annotation, making raw video a source of training signals for geometric, relational, and semantic reasoning.
icml-2026-holi-spatial-evolving-video-st.tldr: Holi-Spatial automatically turns raw videos into reconstructed and annotated 3D scenes that improve vision-language models’ spatial reasoning.

paragraphs: Language models can follow detailed instructions when generating text, but embedding methods often summarize an input using only its final token’s hidden representation. The paper argues that this misses semantic information distributed across the output the model would produce. Generating discrete text and then encoding it again also introduces a discontinuity in the representation process.

InstEmb combines two training objectives. Contrastive learning strengthens information intrinsic to the input through its last-token representation. Representation self-distillation adds output-aware information using learnable look-ahead tokens, without introducing additional decoding latency. These tokens provide a way to incorporate information associated with future output into an embedding rather than requiring ordinary output decoding.

The method also introduces Dual-Anchor Alignment Pooling, designed to match the two complementary training objectives when forming the final representation. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance across multiple instruction-following benchmarks without benchmark-specific supervised data. The result supports jointly training embeddings to capture what the input contains and what an instruction-following model would express in response.
icml-2026-instemb-instruction-following-.tldr: InstEmb improves instruction-following embeddings by combining input representations with output-aware information from learnable look-ahead tokens.

paragraphs: Continual medical image segmentation must incorporate new tasks while retaining earlier capabilities. Tasks from different sources can either benefit from shared learning or interfere with each other. MedCRP-CL addresses the need to discover these relationships as tasks arrive, without assuming a fixed grouping or knowing what future tasks will contain.

The framework uses a Chinese Restaurant Process to infer groups from clinical text prompts, allowing the number of groups to emerge during learning. These semantic modalities incorporate anatomy and pathological context, making them more specific than the imaging modality alone. Each group receives its own LoRA adapter, with within-group EWC regularization supporting retention while dissimilar groups remain parameter-isolated.

The method stores aggregate statistics rather than replaying raw patient data. Across 16 segmentation tasks spanning four imaging modalities, it reports a 73.3% Dice score and 4.1% forgetting, outperforming the best baseline by 8.0% while using six times fewer parameters. The findings support discovering where knowledge should be shared and where separate adaptations can reduce interference.
icml-2026-medcrp-cl-continual-medical-im.tldr: MedCRP-CL discovers related medical segmentation tasks online and assigns group-specific adapters to support transfer while limiting forgetting.

paragraphs: Data attribution assigns value to participants’ contributions to a trained model, informing pricing, audits, and governance. Its usefulness depends on those scores reflecting contribution faithfully. This paper shows that a participant in distributed training can manipulate its measured attribution while leaving the global model’s predictive utility intact.

The attack optimizes latent representations to construct small synthetic batches. It exploits uneven label coverage across participants and sensitivities in the evaluators that measure marginal utility. The objective centers on increasing the participant’s assigned value while preserving the usefulness of the trained model, making attribution manipulation distinct from an attack whose visible effect is lower accuracy.

Across the tested datasets, models, and several marginal-utility evaluators, the attack consistently raises the adversary’s attribution and changes the relative scores of benign clients. It does so without degrading accuracy or triggering the geometry-based defenses evaluated. These findings identify contribution scoring as an attack surface and motivate scoring mechanisms that remain reliable when participants have incentives to manipulate their measured value.
icml-2026-on-the-fragility-of-data-attri.tldr: A distributed-learning participant can inflate its measured data contribution with synthetic batches while preserving model accuracy.

paragraphs: The paper studies an unusually small post-training intervention: entropy minimization using one unlabeled example and roughly ten gradient steps. Entropy measures how spread out a model’s predicted probabilities are, so minimizing it encourages a more concentrated output distribution. The approach is fully unsupervised and does not depend on labeled answers for this update.

To address data contamination, the authors pretrain a seven-billion-parameter language model from scratch using strictly decontaminated data. They report substantial improvements in generation and reasoning across mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning, and coding. The breadth of the reported gains is central to the finding, given the very small amount of data and optimization used.

Their analysis finds a characteristic right-skewed change in logits, the scores underlying token probabilities: high-probability tokens are amplified and low-probability tails suppressed. They distinguish this pattern from reinforcement learning. The findings suggest that the intervention mainly reshapes the model’s output distribution rather than functioning as conventional learning, offering an efficient post-training procedure in the evaluated setting.
icml-2026-one-shot-entropy-minimization-.tldr: Entropy minimization with one unlabeled example and about ten gradient steps improves reasoning by reshaping token probabilities.

paragraphs: Creating and editing presentations requires coordinating text, visual layout, and application controls. PPT-Eval uses this activity to test computer-use agents through 120 PowerPoint tasks across 12 files, organized by difficulty. The tasks cover both creating content and modifying existing presentations, providing a setting where several different finished outputs may be valid.

The paper’s main evaluation challenge is measuring useful but incomplete progress. A binary pass-or-fail score cannot distinguish an agent that completes several requested edits from one that accomplishes very little. PPT-Eval therefore provides a framework for task-specific rubrics that award partial credit, penalize unnecessary changes and poor aesthetics, and return feedback in natural language.

The rubric-based evaluation reaches a Kendall’s tau-b correlation of 0.77 with human judgments. Existing frontier agents still struggle: Claude-4.5-Opus achieves a 45% success rate and a 57% average partial score. Together, these results show why nuanced scoring matters for presentation tasks: it can reflect intermediate accomplishments while preserving the distinction between partial progress and full task completion.
icml-2026-ppt-eval-a-benchmark-for-compu.tldr: PPT-Eval tests agents on 120 PowerPoint tasks using rubrics that capture partial progress, unwanted edits, and presentation aesthetics.

paragraphs: Time-series foundation models typically produce forecasts in a single pass, while regional climate forecasting can benefit from examining several temporal scales and diagnosing systematic errors. RGMR introduces an inference-time framework that brings this structured refinement process to pretrained models. It leaves the backbone parameters frozen, adapting how predictions are refined rather than retraining the underlying model.

The framework uses residual-guided, coarse-to-fine refinement for drought forecasting with the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index. The evaluation covers TimesFM, TimeGPT, and TabPFN at each site, testing whether the approach can work across different backbones. It includes three South Australian sites and three additional regions outside South Australia.

RGMR consistently lowers test-set mean squared error across the evaluated settings. For TimesFM, one-month-ahead prediction error falls by up to 18.9% across the South Australian sites, with an average reduction of approximately 18.7%. The findings support using iterative, multi-resolution refinement as a practical wrapper for frozen forecasting models, with demonstrated architecture independence across the three tested backbones.
icml-2026-residual-guided-multi-resoluti.tldr: RGMR improves drought forecasts by applying residual-guided, coarse-to-fine refinement to frozen time-series foundation models.

paragraphs: Complex diagnosis involves repeated decisions about which tests can distinguish between plausible diseases. Language models can struggle with this interactive process by settling on a diagnosis too early. The paper introduces CompDiag-Bench, which frames diagnosis as sequential decision-making in a dynamic environment where the model requests tests before reaching a final diagnosis.

Salus divides this process among three specialized roles: a Differential Reasoner, a Strategic Controller, and a Workup Proposer. Multi-agent reinforcement learning trains their diagnostic behavior using structured rewards. An LLM judge supplies dense, semantically grounded feedback designed to discourage premature closure and reward accurate differential diagnoses, addressing difficulties caused by sparse or exploitable reward signals.

On the evaluated complex cases, Salus-7B achieves 83.64% Top-1 accuracy, compared with 71.38% for DeepSeek-V3.2 and 80.30% for GPT-5.2. The authors describe its performance as state of the art and on par with GPT-5.2. The result supports coordinating diagnostic reasoning and test selection through specialized roles in the benchmark’s sequential investigation setting.
icml-2026-salus-strategic-diagnostic-tes.tldr: Salus trains specialized agents to coordinate differential diagnosis and sequential testing, reaching 83.64% Top-1 accuracy on evaluated complex cases.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning for language models often updates policies at the level of individual tokens or complete responses. The paper argues that these units can fit reasoning poorly, because a meaningful reasoning step may span several tokens while a full response contains many distinct steps. This mismatch can weaken credit assignment and destabilize multimodal reasoning training.

Segment-Aligned Policy Optimization treats coherent reasoning segments as the units of policy optimization. It formulates a step-wise Markov decision process over those segments, then aligns value estimates, advantage calculations, and importance sampling with their boundaries. The intention is for training signals to correspond more closely to the meaningful steps through which a model develops its answer.

Experiments on representative reasoning benchmarks report consistent improvements over token-level and sequence-level optimization methods. SAPO also shows better training stability and more consistent value estimation alongside significant accuracy gains. These findings support the idea that choosing an update unit aligned with reasoning structure can improve both the learning process and the resulting multimodal reasoning performance.
icml-2026-segment-aligned-policy-optimiz.tldr: SAPO improves multimodal reasoning training by aligning reinforcement-learning updates with coherent reasoning steps.

paragraphs: Dataset distillation creates synthetic training data intended to capture useful information from a larger dataset. Diffusion models provide a generative foundation for this process, but independently updating each synthetic image limits control over the collection as a whole. Set-Coupled Guidance adds an auxiliary controller that coordinates groups of images during generation.

At each diffusion step, SCG supplies feedback that treats the set symmetrically. One component matches set-level statistics to real data using empirical characteristic functions. A second component couples the images’ trajectories through a kernel mechanism to stabilize their joint evolution under noisy feedback. Both operate on lightweight descriptors of predicted clean latents, keeping the added computation low.

The paper provides theoretical analysis of descent and stability for tracking distributional targets. Experiments on ImageNette, ImageWoof, ImageNet-100, and ImageNet-1K show consistent accuracy improvements across multiple diffusion-based baselines. The contribution is a plug-and-play way to optimize relationships within a synthetic dataset during sampling, making the collection itself an explicit target of guidance.
icml-2026-set-coupled-guidance-set-level.tldr: Set-Coupled Guidance coordinates synthetic images during diffusion so the generated training set better matches real-data statistics.

paragraphs: Hypergraphs represent relationships that can involve multiple nodes together, making them useful for complex structured data. Generating synthetic hypergraphs is difficult because their combinatorial structure can make representations computationally unwieldy or cause substantial information loss. SuperHype addresses this representation problem as the foundation of a hypergraph diffusion model.

Its graph-superposition decomposition embeds a hypergraph into a multilayer graph. The authors describe this representation as exact and tractable, retaining generality while enabling manageable computation. A Graph-Superposition Transformer processes the resulting layers as an interconnected sequence. Hypergraph-specific auxiliary features and triplet pooling further help the model incorporate structure and indirect interactions between nodes.

Across five datasets, SuperHype generally reproduces local and global connectivity patterns more faithfully than state-of-the-art baselines. This is a qualified empirical result about structural fidelity, rather than a claim of uniform superiority on every dataset. The broader contribution connects a lossless, tractable representation with a generative architecture designed around that representation, addressing a central obstacle in hypergraph synthesis.
icml-2026-superhype-hypergraph-generatio.tldr: SuperHype uses an exact multilayer graph representation to generate hypergraphs with generally better local and global structural fidelity.

paragraphs: Editing a human-object interaction requires changing a relationship while preserving the relevant person and object. The paper argues that existing benchmarks blur this task with static attribute editing, and that global image metrics miss interaction validity and pair preservation. HOI-Edit addresses this gap with three progressively demanding cognitive levels.

Its HOI-Eval metric uses a vision-language model to reason and answer questions about images with grounded human-object pairs. The authors also evaluate image-to-video models for editing, finding their temporal generation capabilities well suited to changing interactions. Generated videos expose how an attempted edit unfolds, providing a replay that helps diagnose the process behind a failure.

SCPE builds on this diagnosability by iteratively refining prompts that constrain video generation toward the target interaction. Frames extracted from the resulting videos become the final edited images. On HOI-Edit, the framework achieves interaction performance competitive with state-of-the-art image editors such as Nano Banana. The work connects targeted evaluation with a process-based route to self-correcting image edits.
icml-2026-taming-i2v-models-for-image-ho.tldr: HOI-Edit evaluates human-object interaction edits, while SCPE uses iteratively corrected video generation to produce competitive edited images.

paragraphs: Long-context systems often encounter documents that appear relevant but point reasoning in the wrong direction. This paper studies how the proportion of these hard distractors affects performance while holding total context length fixed. It finds a nonlinear pattern: a small initial fraction causes a sharp performance drop, and further increases produce much smaller additional declines.

The authors call this the First Drop of Ink effect. Their theoretical and empirical analysis connects it to attention mechanics: even a small number of hard distractors can capture a disproportionate amount of attention. As their share increases, their additional influence diminishes, explaining why the damage does not grow proportionally with distractor quantity.

Controlled filtering experiments further show that performance gains mainly come from shortening the context rather than removing distractors alone. Substantial recovery occurs only when the hard-distractor proportion approaches zero in these experiments. The findings emphasize upstream retrieval precision: reducing an already large distractor share may leave the system within the region where most of the observed damage has already occurred.
icml-2026-the-first-drop-of-ink-nonlinea.tldr: A small fraction of hard distractors causes most of the observed long-context reasoning damage, with diminishing harm from additional distractors.

paragraphs: Reasoning models benefit from feedback on intermediate steps, but collecting step annotations or running extensive verification is costly. Implicit process rewards use whole-trajectory outcomes instead. The paper identifies a mismatch in log-likelihood-ratio approaches: training constrains an aggregate sequence score, while inference treats its components as meaningful local scores for unfinished reasoning.

IPVRM directly learns the probability of eventual correctness from each partial prefix using outcome labels. Differences between consecutive prefix values supply temporal-difference step signals, aligning what is trained with how rewards are used. The method markedly improves step-verification F1 on ProcessBench, supporting the value of learning prefix-level correctness estimates explicitly.

The paper also introduces Distribution-Level RL, which applies these advantages to sampled tokens and other high-probability candidates without generating additional rollouts. This provides denser updates, but the experiments show that their usefulness depends on reward reliability. Distribution-Level RL delivers limited gains with unreliable implicit rewards and consistently improves downstream reasoning when paired with IPVRM, making reward quality central to the combined approach.
icml-2026-unleashing-implicit-rewards-pr.tldr: IPVRM learns correctness probabilities for reasoning prefixes, enabling reliable step rewards and more effective distribution-level reinforcement learning.
